Research update · 27 October 2026 · complete finite study N2

Clusters can continue; useful learning is still unproven

The policy was updated, and a proposed cluster could supply a later actual move. This held-out panel shows no benefit from training or composition. The trained, untrained and first-move-only controls have the same branch order wherever their saved histories can be compared. The complete small cases take at least as many nodes as lexical search and more total time.

What this experiment establishes

A fresh softmax policy proposes up to four jointly compatible placements, conditioned on the current selected tiles and boundary. A later call can retain an earlier member as a shared attachment and propose a remaining member. The current graph and marking checks validate each proposal again. The ordinary controller still propagates forced moves and chooses each base placement; every ordinary branch remains available. A cluster is a preference, not a proved implication that forces its tail.

The records contain 48 actual later-member placements: 44 during training and four during evaluation. Of these, 29 choose a value other than lexical first; the remaining 19 already agree with lexical first. Learning changes the full proposal contents in 31 of 71 matched observations, but those changes produce no observed branch-order difference from the untrained control. Actual use is therefore established; useful learned transfer is not.

Scope: the palette has 33 fixed XOR-computation Wang types. This phase reuses an explicitly certified 20-layer marking map as one control; it does not learn those markings again from scratch. These finite rectangular unit-anchor models make every required point a generation-zero root. They do not test the general growing frontier, movable boundaries, universal first-order proof tiles, or a learned inventory of mathematical lemmas.

A held-out continuation, with its limitation

The first two inspector choices are consecutive saved observations from the small positive evaluation. At actor call 5, a two-member proposal supplies the next move. At call 6, that first member remains selected and the second member becomes the actual next nonforced placement. The red cross is the scheduled point, and color distinguishes the marking channel and placement role. This same second choice also appears in the first-move-only control: the visible continuation is not evidence that composition improved the search.

    All evaluation cases and controls

    The training words were 000, 011, 101 and 110, with four repetitions and positive/flipped final boundaries. Evaluation uses two different fixed input words. Cases 0 and 1 use 001 on a \(5\times4\) board; cases 2 and 3 use 0010111 on a \(9\times8\) board. Odd cases flip one final symbol. The search windows are five seconds for small evaluations and ten for large evaluations, with 5,000 nodes allowed. These are cooperative limits, not hard interruption guarantees.

    “Seconds” below includes preparation, auditing, verification, lossless encoding and complete evidence writing. It is not raw solver time. SAT means a checked finite exact solution; UNSAT means checked complete exhaustion of this finite problem; UNKNOWN remains unresolved. A common decision prefix does not imply equal status, equal nodes or equal speed.

    What was learned, and what it cost

    All 32 updates change the weight vector, starting from zero. Only the point trajectory supplies the gradient; its reward is tied to the paired checks. Four episodes have a paired verified SAT completion; the other 28 receive UNKNOWN shaping and cost feedback. No timeout is counted as an impossibility proof.

    With verified completion bonus \(I\), verified ordinary-anchor fill fraction \(f\), attempts \(a\), branches \(b\), backtracks \(r\) and actor candidate visits \(v\), the reward is

    \[R=I+0.1f-0.005(a+b+r)-10^{-5}v.\]

    The update uses the token score sum divided by the fixed horizon \(H=4\), learning rate \(0.04\), clipping to \([-4,4]\), and baseline smoothing \(0.2\). The fill denominator is the unseeded ordinary anchors, not the drawn collar. A full generated cluster is paid for even in the first-move-only control.

    Where this leaves the proof-search program

    The next decisive task is an actual fixed, expressive proof palette with a small trusted checker and readable row decoding. Arithmetic and symbolic Hilbert geometry should share this logical core while providing their axioms as input. A benchmark must ask the system to discover proofs without supplied proof scripts, preserve failed and timed-out cases, and compare ordinary search, learned ordering, reusable certified lemmas and parameterized receptor families at the same information and resource budget.

    Useful evidence would be fewer expansions or more newly proved held-out statements after charging for learning, validation and inventory construction. The present conditional clusters are not yet such lemmas. Practical arbitrary-region tiling, movable boundaries, Turtle on the \(A_2\) lattice and Penrose arithmetic over \(\mathbb Z[\zeta_5]\) remain open research goals. A substitution rule is one possible tool, not a required endpoint.

    Research update · 27 October 2026 · independently reviewed complete run

    Local failures become twenty reusable marking layers

    The new run completed and passed whole-evidence review. Starting with no learned corner markings, it regenerated the complete local pair catalogue, proved the failed local completions, and encoded those failures in \(20\) literal marking channels. Both small boundary problems finished with no branching after the markings were added. On the completed small cases, the conventional CSP control given the same information followed the same complete search traces. All larger-board arms remained unknown at their declared windows.

    This is a finite constraint-learning result on a supplied computation palette. It supplies no new arithmetic or geometry theorem, reinforcement learning policy, universal proof palette, tile-cluster inventory or plane-tiling proof. The earlier failed attempt remains unadmitted; its outputs were not used to seed this fresh run.

    What was learned

    The inventory contains \(33\) fixed Wang types, placed by translation only. The experiment tests all \(4\cdot33^2=4\,356\) ordered type-pair classes at axial or diagonal offsets. Each nonconflicting pair is fixed in its smallest free rectangular box, at most \(2\times2\) cells, with the full palette available in every remaining cell. These are local completion tests; they are not the master algorithm’s growing-frontier or one-corona experiment.

    Fresh local testsComplete certificatesShared negative familiesLiteral point assignmentsMatched search controls

    The catalogue contains \(1\,779\) original Wang edge conflicts, \(831\) locally completable pairs and \(1\,746\) failed completions, with no unresolved label. A separately authored CSP checker validates complete SAT or UNSAT certificates. After each negative label, a dedicated marking fragment is recorded. Once the entire catalogue is resolved, the factorizer shares marking channels across families of negatives.

    For one diagonal, let \(N\) be its negative-pair relation. A family chooses sets \(Z\) and \(O\) with \(Z\times O\subseteq N\). All types in \(Z\) assign \(0\) at one corner; types in \(O\) assign \(1\) at the opposite corner on the same channel. Their translated corners coincide, so a forbidden pair immediately disagrees. An omitted assignment is absent, distinct from the literal \(0\). All actual contacts of the final map were independently reconstructed: their union is exactly the learned negative relation, with no additional conflict.

    All families and the finite bound

    The factorizer takes a row with the most uncovered negatives, closes its neighbor columns against the original negative relation, emits the resulting biclique, and removes covered pairs. Each chosen row is cleared permanently. Thus the human-authored argument gives at most \(33\) families per diagonal, or \(66\) overall. The actual run used \(10\) per diagonal. This is a termination and coverage bound, with no minimum-channel or optimum claim.

    Cost and scientific assessment

    Fresh labeling took \(161.63\,\mathrm{s}\). The actual factorizer call took \(0.0203\,\mathrm{s}\); the broader dedicated-map, factorization, output and independent-check phase took \(1.357\,\mathrm{s}\). These are different intervals, not an additive cost partition. The parent’s interval from immediately before child launch through its owned wait was \(369.44\,\mathrm{s}\); the child lifetime RSS high-water mark after wait was \(204\,800\,000\) bytes. The study retained \(167\,616\,315\) bytes of named worker outputs. Whole-run evidence includes qualification, labeling, auditing, serialization and I/O.

    The concrete contribution is certified failure learning and compact geometric encoding. On the completed cases it improves propagation over original edge constraints. A conventional solver given identical learned information receives the same benefit and makes the same decisions. There is currently no evidence here of a GCTS-specific search advantage, competitive theorem-proving performance, or an RL contribution. The earlier manual STATE layer and this fresh learned layer are distinct experiments.

    The next useful test is a validated inventory of multi-step clusters with explicit receptor interfaces, measured against conventional reusable-lemma and macro-action controls. It must learn useful choices on separate training contexts, retain the base-placement fallback, and report success and cost on declared evaluation contexts. Improving runtime auditing and evidence handling can make that experiment feasible; the present audit-heavy timeouts do not isolate solver cost.

    Algorithm conformance, transfer scope and evidence boundary

    This is the finite unit-anchor specialization of the shared algorithm: all required points are roots at generation \(0\); ordinary placements have generation \(1\). The complete frontier-point/candidate incidence graph is maintained. Global dead ends and forced moves precede branching; earliest generation is primary and candidate count only breaks its ties. Assigned marking values are compared at every shared point, including points outside the positive-support region. UNSAT and unknown returns restore the entry state internally. A SAT return retains its witness; the worker then explicitly rolls back and checks the exact entry state. These restoration checks cover markings, reference counts, exclusions, generations and both incidence directions.

    The free-box certificates justify transfer to completely filled rectangles using the same palette, including extra boundary restrictions. A failed diagonal completion needs an intermediate cell present in the rectangle. The current argument does not cover arbitrary holes or nonrectangular regions. No holdout claim is made: every resolved pair class in the catalogue is available to the factorizer. Full runtime states were independently checked; main benchmark traces retain all semantic event digests, not the entire snapshot history. Qualification retains complete snapshot histories. Each complete arm body is written and read back before the next begins.

    The ZIP contains the complete selected evidence for this one current run: all raw outputs and certificates, authenticated runtime Sources, exact plan and consumed authority, owned tool and worker captures, complete review records and supporting static evidence. A catalogue gives every member’s original path, byte count and SHA256. The external Python executable is identified by its complete raw pin and is not included. Older published studies remain in their separate archives; later publication, deployment and browser receipts are outside this archive’s preparation boundary. No scientific call was replayed during the post-run review.

    The broader GCTS+RL and proof-search program remains active. The original Turtle and Penrose objectives, arbitrary-region and movable-boundary work, genuine multiscale clusters, and arithmetic and symbolic Hilbert-geometry proof discovery remain open.

    What a generated marking looks like

    The figure renders the first generated failure fragment, PAIR_PROOF:2181, from the saved arrival log. It is an illustration of unadmitted output from this failed study. The small square outlines help read the Wang encoding; the engine uses positive-support centers and assigned point values. No rotations are allowed.

    Read this local obstruction in ordinary mathematical language
    1. The upper-left tile is \(A=C(\#,\#,\#)\); the lower-right tile is \(B=C(\#,0,\#)\). Their diagonal displacement is \(d=(1,1)\).
    2. The input/output cap tiles cannot fill the upper-right cell because their lateral labels do not match A's east label, P:#:#.
    3. A computation tile \(C(a,b,c)\) filling that cell would have to satisfy \(a=b=\#\), by its west label. Its south label is then S:#, by the palette definition.
    4. B requires S:0 on its north side. The labels disagree, so no upper-right tile exists. The saved support record lists all \(33\) alternatives; none passes there.
    5. The generated fragment assigns opposite binary literals at the shared corner. Future copies of this pair can therefore conflict through ordinary marking agreement. This paragraph is a human explanation of the stored local example, not a newly admitted theorem-discovery result.

    The transfer argument assumes a fully filled rectangular board: the pair's bounding box must also be filled. Arbitrary regions with holes or missing corner cells require separate justification.

    Assessment and next experiment

    This attempt supplies no evidence of a GCTS search advantage. Its useful engineering lessons are that pair-specific channels need more efficient shared structure, and complete per-arm evidence must be saved immediately. The current code accumulated benchmark returns in memory until the whole matrix finished; those returns are missing from this failed packet. There is no substitute benchmark table here.

    The next design will separate local discovery and certification from individually budgeted matched searches, keep the same constraints and decision policy in both point and CSP controls, and persist each arm before starting the next. A bounded small comparison should finish before increasing the board size. The longer-term question remains whether reusable, certified marking or receptor-cluster inventories reduce total work across problems. RL cluster proposals, a fixed first-order proof palette, symbolic Hilbert geometry and practical Turtle/Penrose growth remain open program goals.

    Research update · 27 October 2026 · independently checked finite experiments

    Certified extended markings eliminated branching in two finite tests

    The mechanism worked on this small example. With the same Wang tiles, boundary conditions and GCTS search engine, adding a proved redundant STATE layer removed all branch decisions on both a solvable tableau and an impossible final boundary. The layer was designed by hand. This experiment does not yet use learned markings, RL, receptor clusters or mathematical theorem discovery.

    Each boundary problem has \(20\) ordinary cells, \(33\) tile types at every cell and \(18\) fixed collar seeds: \(678\) candidate placements on \(38\) required points. An independent routine examined all \(19\,683\) guarded symbol histories in each arm. The solvable context has one complete solution; the impossible context has none. All four search runs and the separate API qualification passed complete independent review.

    Rows retain the predeclared execution order: positive baseline, positive STATE, negative STATE, negative baseline. Nodes count search decisions, including terminal decisions. The positive STATE prediction—\(21\) nodes, \(20\) forced placements and no branches or backtracks—was fixed before the run and matched in every declared field. There was no negative counter prediction. Every recorded event was reviewed, including failed branches and contextual exclusions, and every run restored its complete starting state.

    Timing is descriptive. These are single fresh-process observations. The late worker sample includes loading, construction, validation, exhaustive reference histories, search with all audits, verification, evidence preparation and full result serialization, writing, fsync, readback and hashing. Its clock begins at worker main entry after interpreter and module startup; the final budget check, terminal encoding, flushing and shutdown follow the sample. Different audit counts mean different validation work. No statistical speedup, practical advantage or superiority to other proof-search systems is established.

    The separate API qualification exercised \(30\) malformed-input controls and full augmentation/erasure and input-detachment checks, without instantiating the search engine or calling solve. The pure compile_wang construction was included. Its costs are reported separately. The four search runs retained \(224\) stable audits in total. The download contains the complete scientific outputs, rather than only the successful tiling or selected counters.

    What the extra geometric layer does

    STATE connects a computation tile to the three symbols it reads in the preceding row, including points outside its square. In a complete legal tableau, the original Wang rules already imply these agreements. The certified augmentation preserves every original placement, translation, positive-support value, WANG assignment, required point and seed; erasing STATE gives the entire original model exactly. The new channel contributes \(2\,280\) assignments at \(33\) static slots across the inventory. The added agreements can reveal a conflict in a partial placement sooner, which removes candidates through the maintained point–candidate graph.

    The actual positive tiling also passed the whole augmented point check before projection to the original Wang tableau and its symbol trace. For the negative cases there is no selected full tiling or inverse trace; those conditional fields stay empty or null. Empty reference sets are not treated as a general proof of learned nogoods.

    Algorithm conformance and the limits of this test

    This is a finite, translation-only specialization. All required points begin at root generation \(0\), and ordinary placements have generation \(1\). Both complete incidence directions are maintained; global dead ends and forced moves take priority over branching. The audit checks include marking-only dependencies outside the positive-support domain and exact rollback of markings, reference counts, generations, exclusions and both graphs. This does not test a growing infinite frontier, plane tiling, movable boundaries, learned cluster proposals or multiscale lemma construction.

    The extra channel is a manually certified redundant constraint representation. A useful next control is a conventional constraint solver given the same STATE information, followed by larger held-out contexts and markings learned from failures with preservation certificates. Receptor families and reusable proof clusters remain research goals. A single universal proof palette and automatic discovery of arithmetic or Hilbert-geometry theorems have not been demonstrated by this experiment.

The earlier phrase “Complete observed worker lifetime” was too broad: the process-creation call and child work before its return are excluded. Worker main-entry and observer supervision clocks have different startup exclusions and must not be subtracted to estimate startup cost.

    Four tile rows encode three state rows

    The main input has width \(5\) and two transitions. Its saved state trace is

    \[a^{(0)}=\mathtt{\#100\#}\quad\longrightarrow\quad a^{(1)}=\mathtt{\#010\#}\quad\longrightarrow\quad a^{(2)}=\mathtt{\#101\#}.\]

    The Wang board has an input-cap row, two computation rows and an output-cap row: \(5\times4=20\) selected ordinary tiles. The output cap checks the final state; it does not add another state transition.

    Colors identify exact literal strings, not numerical weights or learned classes. Shared midpoint assignments must agree literally. The full key is:

    I:#I:0I:1O:#O:0O:1P:#:#P:#:0P:#:1P:0:#P:0:0P:0:1P:1:#P:1:0P:1:1ROW:BOTROW:TOPS:#S:0S:1

    The base model uses \(L=\mathbb{Z}^{2}\). A cell at \((x,y)\) has positive support only at \((2x,2y)\); its marks lie at \((2x\pm1,2y)\) and \((2x,2y\pm1)\). These mark-only points contribute no positive support. Only translations in the explicit finite placement universe are allowed. The complete main model contains \(660\) ordinary candidates, \(18\) mandatory collar seeds and \(38\) required anchor points.     Read the supplied table as a local rule

    Let \(\beta(\#)=\beta(\mathtt{0})=0\) and \(\beta(\mathtt{1})=1\). For left, center and right symbols \((\ell,s,r)\), a center wall stays a wall. Otherwise the next symbol is the exclusive-or of the two neighbors:

    \[f(\ell,s,r)=\begin{cases}\#,&s=\#,\\ \mathtt{0},&s\ne\#\text{ and }\beta(\ell)=\beta(r),\\ \mathtt{1},&s\ne\#\text{ and }\beta(\ell)\ne\beta(r).\end{cases}\]

    Both endpoint guards stay fixed, with wall symbols immediately outside the word. This formula describes the supplied primary table. The alternate control supplies a different table by changing only \(f(\#,\mathtt{1},\#)\) from \(\mathtt{0}\) to \(\mathtt{1}\). It is not an inferred rule or a learned marking.

Complete rollback and the distinction between unknown and exhaustion were part of the checks.

    One branch forces the neighboring Wang tile

    This is a recorded result from Wang-alternating-labels. Both cells initially admit either tile type. The engine chooses Tile X on the left; matching at the shared marking point leaves Tile Y as the sole candidate on the right.

    1. Choose Tile X. The left required point has two candidates, so this is a genuine branch decision.
    2. Propagate the shared value. Tile X on the right would assign b to the occupied shared mark. That candidate is removed; Tile Y assigns a and becomes forced.
    3. Check and undo. The complete point solution and original Wang assignment pass their independent checks. The explicit rollback then restores both original candidate domains.

    These colors define the small Wang problem. Learning additional useful markings, and compiling a mathematical theorem and its proof checker into such a palette, are still future steps.

    A distant marking updates every affected frontier edge

    A separate recorded point control exercises the extended marking support. Tile A assigns literal 0 at \((1000,1000)\); Tile B assigns literal 1 at the same slot and covers both of the later roots. Neither marking adds coverage at that distant point.

    Recorded stateRoot \((0,0)\)Root \((1,0)\)Root \((2,0)\)
    Initial domains\(\{A\}\)\(\{B,C\}\)\(\{B,D\}\)
    After forced Tile AFilled\(\{C\}\)\(\{D\}\)
    After forced Tiles C and DFilledFilledFilled

    The single marking disagreement removes the shared candidate B from both frontier domains. The saved solution is \(\{A,C,D\}\), and rollback restores the original domains and the unassigned marking slot. This directly exercises the point/candidate dependency graph. These marking values were authored as part of the control; no marking was learned in this run.

    Mathematical analysis · agent-derived reasoning

    Representation result with a clear limit. Any finite list of forbidden translated pairs has an exact finite equality-marking encoding under the stated assumptions. A genuinely higher-order exclusion cannot always be represented on unchanged fixed tile states. These are elementary mathematical arguments, reviewed by a separate agent and Root; they are not experimental engine discoveries or machine-checked proofs.

    Distant markings can reject a pair with disjoint base support

    Abstract construction from mathematical reasoning. This diagram was authored by the agent to explain a representation lemma. It is not an executed fixture, learned model, experimental search result or automatically discovered proof. It illustrates partial legality only. No fixed target, completed tiling, plane construction, extension or performance claim is made. The host reader supplies its established MathJax renderer; this fragment adds no scripts.

    Work on \(L=\mathbb Z\), with translations only and two fixed types. Put \(t_A=t_B=\delta_0\), where \(\delta_0(p)=\mathbf1_{\{0\}}(p)\). In one fresh channel \(\gamma\), assign \(m_{A,\gamma}(0)=0\) and \(m_{B,\gamma}(-3)=1\), leaving all other slots unassigned. Thus a translated \(B\)-placement at \(y\) places its marking value at \(y-3\), although its positive base support is at \(y\).

    • Positive base support, value \(t=1\)
    • Assigned marking value \(0\)
    • Assigned marking value \(1\)
    • Lattice point with no placed positive base support

    The two drawing lanes show different data at the same horizontal lattice coordinates. They are display lanes, not extra lattice dimensions. Gray circles carry base values. Colored circles carry marking values in the single channel. Two concentric colored rings denote unequal assignments at one common point.

    Rejected pair: \(\{(A,0),(B,3)\}\)

    Marking lane

    \(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)\(3\)\(4\)

    Base lane and lattice coordinates

    \[0=3-3,\qquad m_{A,\gamma}(0)=0\ne1=m_{B,\gamma}(-3).\]

    Both placements assign at point \(0\), with unequal values in channel \(\gamma\). The pair is marking-inconsistent. Its base supports \(\{0\}\) and \(\{3\}\) are disjoint, so \(T_S(p)\le1\) everywhere before the marking test.

    Compatible pair: \(\{(A,0),(B,4)\}\)

    Marking lane

    \(-1\)\(0\)\(1\)\(2\)\(3\)\(4\)

    Base lane and lattice coordinates

    \[4-3=1\ne0.\]

    The \(A\)-marking is assigned at \(0\); the translated \(B\)-marking is assigned at \(1\). No point receives unequal assigned values. Point \(1\) is a mark-only point for this pair: it adds no base capacity or coverage obligation. The base supports \(\{0\}\) and \(\{4\}\) are disjoint, so this pair is a legal marked partial state.

    The sign is essential: placing the second prototype’s marking at \(-3\) encodes the relative offset \(d=3\). Missing values impose no equality test. The construction compares point values; it does not use polygon intersections, regions between the points, or visual overlap of drawn shapes as a legality rule.

    What finite equality markings can represent

    Provenance and scope. This is an elementary mathematical proof derived by the agent, not a proof discovered or checked by the experimental search engine. It belongs to mathematical analysis, outside automated-discovery and benchmark counts. No experimental data, private implementation, learned model or runtime proof object was used. The fragment uses the host reader’s established MathJax delimiters and adds no script dependency. Colors below are reader annotations, not learned GCTS markings.

    The exact pair representation is possible under translation-only, fixed-type, distinct-placement semantics. It does not represent arbitrary higher-order exclusions, prove complete tilability, or imply useful search speed.

    Model and statement

    Let \(L\cong\mathbb Z^r\) be a discrete additive lattice and \(I\) a finite set of prototype types. Fix exact finite-support base functions \(t_i:L\to[0,1]\). A placement is \((i,x)\), and each placement identity is selected at most once. For a finite set \(S\), write

    \[T_S(p)=\sum_{(i,x)\in S}t_i(p-x).\]

    Base partial capacity legality means \(T_S(p)\le1\) everywhere. A channel marking \(m_{i,\gamma}:D_{i,\gamma}\to\{0,1\}\) is a coherent partial function with finite domain. Its translated value at \(x+u\) is \(m_{i,\gamma}(u)\). Only values assigned at the same point and channel are compared. Missing is unconstrained; assigned \(0\) is a value. The base data stay fixed.

    A finite set \(F\subset I\times I\times L\) forbids distinct placements \((i,x)\ne(j,y)\) when \((i,j,y-x)\in F\). A descriptor denotes every admitted translation of its pair. The descriptions \((i,j,d)\) and \((j,i,-d)\) denote the same unordered physical exclusion.

    Representation theorem. There are finitely many binary equality channels and finite marking supports such that, for every finite placement set,

    \[ \operatorname{Legal}_{t,m}(S) \iff [\,\forall p,\ T_S(p)\le1\,]\ \land\ [\,\nexists (i,x)\ne(j,y)\in S:\ (i,j,y-x)\in F\,]. \]

    This is an equivalence for partial legality. It makes no assertion that such a partial state extends, fills a target, or tiles an infinite domain.

    Construction and complete proof

    Close the descriptors under \((i,j,d)\mapsto(j,i,-d)\), discard the vacuous \((i,i,0)\) descriptors, and choose one representative per remaining reciprocal orbit. Call the finite representative set \(R\) and put \(q=|R|\). For each \(f=(A,B,d)\in R\), make one private channel \(\gamma_f\) with just

    \[ m_{A,\gamma_f}(0)=0,\qquad m_{B,\gamma_f}(-d)=1. \]

    Leave every other slot in that channel unassigned. If \(A=B\), both entries belong to that one prototype, and \(d\ne0\) makes their domain points distinct.

    1. If \(A\ne B\), an \(A\)-placement at \(x\) assigns \(0\) at \(x\), while a \(B\)-placement at \(y\) assigns \(1\) at \(y-d\). A disagreement occurs exactly when \(x=y-d\), or \(y-x=d\). Placements of the same type assign only equal values in this channel. Other types assign nothing. Thus this channel rejects exactly its declared pair orbit.

    2. If \(A=B\), each placement at \(x\) assigns \(0\) at \(x\) and \(1\) at \(x-d\). It is internally coherent. Distinct translations \(x,y\) can disagree only through \(x=y-d\) or \(x-d=y\); these give \(y-x=d\) or \(y-x=-d\). These are precisely the same unordered same-type exclusion. Equal-value overlaps do not reject anything.

    3. The cross-type argument also covers \(d=0\): different types are rejected exactly at equal translations. The same-type case \(d=0\) is vacuous for two distinct placements and is omitted. The literal double assignment there would not be a function.

    4. Every forbidden pair therefore creates a disagreement in its representative channel. Conversely, a marking inconsistency has two unequal values at one point and channel. Coherence of each prototype implies that two distinct placements supplied them; the preceding analysis identifies a declared pair orbit. Different private channels never compare with one another, even if their spatial supports overlap. Hence the conjunction creates exactly the desired exclusions.

    5. The unchanged capacity condition conjoined with this marking equivalence is exactly the theorem. There are \(q\) channels and \(2q\) assigned prototype-channel-point slots. The supports are finite, but may lie far outside positive base support. This is a representation-size bound, not an optimality or runtime bound.

    The precise caveat. No counterexample exists under the stated distinct-pair assumptions. If \((A,A,0)\) instead means “ban even one \(A\)-placement,” the assertion is false for coherent equality markings: a base-legal singleton cannot disagree with another placement. For example, \(t_A=\mathbf1_{\{0\}}\) on \(L=\mathbb Z\) has a legal singleton. Likewise, an order-sensitive relation on a sequence is not legality of a placement set. The minus sign in the construction matters: it produces \(y-x=d\), not the opposite cross-type offset.

    The converse exposes unwanted pair exclusions

    Every fixed finite-channel, finite-support equality marking also has an exact finite effective pair list:

    \[ F_m=\{(i,j,u-v): \exists\gamma,\ u\in D_{i,\gamma},\ v\in D_{j,\gamma},\ m_{i,\gamma}(u)\ne m_{j,\gamma}(v)\}. \]

    The list is finite. Two translated assignments meet exactly when \(x+u=y+v\), equivalently \(y-x=u-v\); unequal values then give precisely a pair in this list. A coherent prototype cannot generate a same-type zero-offset conflict. Thus finite fixed equality markings describe exactly finite translation-invariant pair exclusions, relative to the unchanged capacity rule. Compressing or fitting markings can create extra difference offsets; preserving sampled contacts alone does not prove those additional exclusions sound.

    Conditional corollary: certified pairs give redundant markings

    Fix the same original base model and context \(\mathcal C\), including admitted placements, required points, boundary or exterior data, seeds, inventory and solution meaning. Suppose every pair in the finite list, at every admitted translation, is separately proved impossible in any original exact solution.

    Then the constructed markings preserve exactly the solution set in \(\mathcal C\). Every original solution avoids the proved-impossible pairs, and the construction rejects no unlisted pair, so its markings agree. Conversely, forgetting the added markings leaves the identical original base problem. For an infinite solution whose original pointwise conditions are already well-defined, any marking conflict would still be witnessed by two placements, giving the same argument. This is equality of solution sets, possibly empty; it proves neither existence nor infinite extension.

    Capacity-legal partial states containing an unextendible pair may now be rejected. The corollary preserves complete original solutions, not every base-legal partial state.

    A rooted proof transfers only when translation is a proved automorphism of the same context and solution family, or when all relevant translations are separately covered. In the invariant case, translating a hypothetical solution back gives a contradiction at the rooted pair. Fixed boundaries or seeds can defeat that argument. Translating the context as well does not establish a claim in the original context.

    No current corona label or finite-window failure is asserted to meet this premise. Budget exhaustion is unknown; boundary-dependent negatives and incomplete enumeration are not global proofs. A geometric reading also needs a faithful reduction to the point model. The corollary gives a possible route to certified failure markings, with no extra pair exclusions, and makes no claim about compactness or measured benefit.

    Why a genuine triple exclusion is different

    Fixed-state limitation. Suppose a triple \(S=\{c_1,c_2,c_3\}\) is base-capacity-legal and all its constituent pairs have consistent markings. At each point and channel, any two assigned values come from one coherent placement or from a compatible pair. They must agree. The entire union is therefore a partial function, so the triple is marking-consistent and hence legal. The argument works for any finite collection and does not depend on binary values or finite support.

    A triple that markings cannot isolate

    Take \(L=\mathbb Z\), types \(A,B,C\), and \(t_A=t_B=t_C=\tfrac13\mathbf1_{\{0\}}\). The coincident pair sums are \(\tfrac23\), while the coincident triple sum is \(1\). Require \(\{(A,x),(B,x),(C,x)\}\) to be forbidden while every constituent pair stays allowed.

    The triple is base-legal. Any fixed equality marking allowing those pairs also allows the triple. Thus this higher-order rule has no exact representation in the stated marking model.

    A triple already rejected by capacity

    With \(t_A=t_B=t_C=\tfrac12\mathbf1_{\{0\}}\), each coincident pair sums to \(1\), but the triple sums to \(\tfrac32>1\).

    Capacity itself rejects the triple, with no markings. The limitation therefore requires the triple to be base-capacity-legal; pairwise capacity legality alone does not suffice.

    These are abstract mathematical examples, not executed fixtures. Pair allowance concerns the same fixed markings and placement identities. Separate existential choices of auxiliary states for each pair are outside the hypothesis. Added contextual or auxiliary states can change expressive power, but their projection to the original problem needs a separate soundness and completeness proof.

    Consequences for the original GCTS architecture

    Representation and certification must stay separate. Problem-defining exclusions change the problem; sample-supported exclusions remain hypotheses unless proved redundant. A higher-order failure clause or receptor-family cluster relation cannot simply be renamed a fixed marking on unchanged original types while preserving all constituent pairs. Retain a justified higher-order constraint or prove an enlarged state encoding. Ordinary symbolic proof-DAG relations do not automatically become point-placement markings.

    Clusters must expand to distinct base placements with exact aggregate base values and compatible marking union; shared constituents cannot be double-counted. Keep complete base-placement fallback, the complete frontier/candidate graph, global dead-end checks, global forced propagation, then earliest-generation branching. A proposal pool cannot establish candidate degrees or forced moves.

    All assigned marking points and channels, including distant mark-only points outside the frontier, must participate in candidate dependencies. They do not create base capacity, coverage obligations or generation births. Marking rejections must propagate globally through the graph. Trail values, reference counts, candidate validity and incidences for exact rollback; version frozen exclusions and revalidate the prefix, graph, caches and trails when rules change.

    The explicit construction can grow to \(q\) channels and \(2q\) assignment slots with distant support. Their storage and update cost may outweigh pruning. This elementary boundary gives no universal encoding, compact optimum, useful speed, fit, geometric GCTS conformance, learned transfer or trained RL benefit.

    For an already-marked input model, extend the argument with a disjoint namespace of new channels. No current learned exclusion list is certified by this mathematical note.

    What this contributes

    Automatic acquisition now produces a more varied, parameterized inventory with exact primitive expansions and source maps. Schema inference and lemma reuse are established symbolic methods. This result does not show that GCTS or RL is doing the proof search, matching another prover, or surpassing one. No new arithmetic or Hilbert-geometry benchmark theorem was searched in this experiment.

    The next test is contextual use: supply real proofs for boundary ports, expand only genuinely selected applications into the final proof, retain primitive fallback, and give the conventional lemma/CD control the same acquired information. The frozen evaluation target remains unopened and unsearched. No easier target or supplied intermediate lemma is introduced.

    Current research · manual transfer audit · 24 October 2026 UTC

    A checked fragment still needs somewhere useful to attach

    The four-family inventory below is valid for its checked source instances. Before spending the untouched evaluation target, we examined whether those families could attach to its goal or subformulas. The answer is no for that particular search interface. This is a manually derived size obstruction, independently checked from the saved patterns and the already declared input bounds; the evaluation formula was not opened or searched.

    First donor families

    \(49\)

    Minimum expanded formula nodes in either family output.

    Second donor families

    \(64\)

    Minimum expanded formula nodes in either family output.

    Evaluation goal

    \(15\)

    Declared maximum expanded nodes. Every goal subformula is at most this large.

    Why a direct backward match is impossible

    Using the display aliases in the original report below, every current family concludes

    \[V_i=\bigl(D_i\to(D_i\to D_i)\bigr)\to(D_i\to D_i).\]

    There are five occurrences of \(D_i\) and four further implication nodes. The donor skeletons remain rigid even though their atom parameters can be replaced by whole formulas. Every formula image contains at least one node, so

    \[|D_0|_{\min}=9,\qquad |D_1|_{\min}=12,\qquad |V_0|_{\min}=5\cdot9+4=49,\quad |V_1|_{\min}=5\cdot12+4=64.\]

    Equal substitutions do not merge repeated syntax occurrences. Since \(15<49<64\), exact structural matching cannot attach any output to the evaluation goal or one of its subformulas. The initial hypothesis context is empty. We therefore retain the target unspent instead of timing a predetermined zero-match experiment.

    Scope of this result. It rules out the goal/subformula interface for this inventory. Search can introduce larger auxiliary formulas, and primitive proof reconstruction can expose larger obligations. Neither possibility has been tested here. This is not a non-provability result or a general limitation of lemma reuse.

    Generalize the proof structure, then check every inference

    The next component infers formula parameters from a fragment's axiom and inference structure, rather than retaining every connective of its donor. It gives each boundary formula and logical-axiom witness slot fresh variables, reconstructs each axiom schema, and solves the ordered modus ponens equations with first-order unification and an occurs check. It must then verify the generic equations and specialize back to every original formula, witness and source occurrence.

    Keep the proof graphPreserve each internal row, boundary port and ordered reference.
    Fresh formula slotsSeparate accidental donor equalities from required schema structure.
    Solve constraintsRebuild axioms and unify every modus ponens equation; reject cycles.
    Check the resultVerify the symbolic proof and every source specialization.

    This is a design diagram. It is not a new measured acquisition result, learned GCTS marking, or finite Wang-tile construction. The new schema-inference algorithm has not been executed.

    A small manual example, and why it still does not settle transfer

    The closed fragment has an H1 row, an H2 row and one application of modus ponens. Write independent axiom variables first:

    \[X\to(Y\to X),\qquad \bigl(A\to(B\to C)\bigr)\to\bigl((A\to B)\to(A\to C)\bigr).\]

    Matching the first row to the second row's antecedent requires \(X=A=C\) and \(Y=B\), giving the schematic consequence

    \[(A\to B)\to(A\to A).\]

    This manual derivation is a prospective expectation for the implementation, not a newly discovered machine proof. Its minimum size is only \(7\) nodes. Nevertheless, every instance contains the proper tautological subformula \(A\to A\). The evaluation input rules exclude proper tautological subformulas, so this closed schema still cannot match its goal or subformulas.

    The conditional fragment can have arbitrary output \(C\), but it requires a prior proof of \((A\to(B\to A))\to C\). Its antecedent is an H1 theorem, so this boundary requirement is equivalent to proving \(C\); the boundary cannot be treated as a free fact. Useful transfer still needs a suitable contextual or auxiliary-obligation search interface and a more useful inventory.

    Connection to existing proof search

    Inferring theorem schemas from proof structures is established territory. Wernhard's Generating Theorems by Generating Proof Structures (2026) uses condensed detachment and studies lemma synthesis through proof DAG compression, with a benchmark converted from Metamath. Earlier work on compressed combinatory proof structures (2022) connects principal types, formula unification and reusable proof structure. CD Tools and SGCD provide a relevant conventional comparison.

    Our inference component belongs to that conventional symbolic layer. A GCTS contribution would require additional evidence that receptor constraints improve the search, and an RL contribution would require a trained proposal or selection policy tested against a matched control. Schema inference and a colored proof display alone establish neither.

    Next evidence required. Implement and independently review schema inference; declare a broader acquisition policy and a shared contextual demand interface before evaluation. Give ordinary lemma reuse the same acquired information, retain primitive fallback, trace each used cluster into the complete checked final proof, and charge matching, expansion and checking costs. The existing inventory and frozen target remain unchanged.

    Current result · finite inventory admitted · 24 October 2026 UTC

    Four automatically acquired proof families

    A proved limitation of the current selection rule

    The rule considers reachable proof roots in increasing source-row order, grows a fragment by adding its least external predecessor, and keeps the first two distinct eligible family keys per donor. Although fragments of up to eight internal nodes are allowed, this policy selects only two- and three-node fragments on a closed propositional proof containing just logical axioms and modus ponens, or selects none. Root's argument has received independent manual review; this is an analysis of the search policy, not a theorem found by the proof-search engine.

    Why this matters. This version can test the bridge from a primitive proof to a typed family and a checked instance. It cannot demonstrate acquisition of larger clusters, internal DAG sharing or multiscale proof structure. The source implementation keeps the declared policy. A later diversity policy needs its own declaration before its results are observed.

    Schematic dependency cells, with fixed orientation. Purple marks an internal axiom, teal an external boundary premise and amber the inference. The picture assumes the antecedent is the earlier of the two parents; exchanging their source order leaves the argument unchanged. These are explanatory cells, not an implementation of a fixed finite Wang palette.

    Read the argument line by line
    1. If no modus ponens row reaches the final conclusion, every reachable root is an axiom with no predecessors. Growth cannot reach the minimum size, so no family is selected.
    2. Otherwise let \(r\) be the earliest reachable modus ponens row, with predecessors \(a,b<r\). Both predecessors reach the conclusion. Either being modus ponens would contradict the choice of \(r\), so both are axioms.
    3. The parents are distinct: using the same row as antecedent and implication would require a finite formula \(F\) with \(F=(F\to C)\), impossible by syntax-tree size.
    4. Earlier axiom roots produce no eligible fragment. At \(r\), growth first adds \(\min(a,b)\), producing two internal rows and one boundary port. Adding the other parent produces three internal rows and no boundary ports. Both prefixes satisfy the declared structural limits.
    5. The full keys differ because their internal-node lists have different lengths. They fill the quota immediately. No larger or internally shared fragment is acquired. Overlap between the two saved fragments is distinct from sharing within one fragment.

    The argument assumes finite propositional formula trees, backward references, and only the supported axiom and modus ponens rules in the final row's ancestor closure. A later encoder or resource refusal means a stopped library attempt; it does not authorize silently skipping to later fragments.
